scope_summary:
Source-verification ledger for the forces in build f10fe585 (origin/main 43e3e5b). 42 entries in docs/audit-post8-evidence/sources-oob/ledger.md and ledger.json (generated by tools/audit-post8/sources-oob/make-ledger.py). Covered: both army totals; all 37 numeric strengths, each compared with at least one source; the strength notes; the claims named in the brief (decisions 184, 202 (b), 210 (c), 213 (b)); a sample of commanders and compositions; four dress claims (French line infantry, Russian musketeers, Austrian line infantry, Szekler hussars); four of the eleven ORDNANCE claims, including the drivers inference.

How it was checked: I read the cited material myself on page images (Schönhals 1873 pp. 177-178; Sokolov 2006 t. II pp. 183-200; Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky 1844 p. 178; the 30th Bulletin, Corr. t. XI p. 450; Gassendi 1809; Alombert t. I and t. IV; Fieffé 1854; Viskovatov). For Duffy 1977, a lending item whose pages cannot be opened here, I used archive.org's full-text search of the OCR. As a calibration, that search reproduces exactly the Russian Guard rows that register S5.7 read on the owner's photograph.

Verdicts: 14 verified, 17 partly, 7 contradicted, 2 not supported, 2 inaccessible.

Main results:
- Six order-of-battle figures are attributed to Duffy, but Duffy does not print them (III Corps detachment, Friant, Kienmayer, Dokhturov, IV Column, Russian wing).
- The III Corps detachment and the IV Column are drawn below every figure in the sources the project can read, and their notes omit those figures.
- Seven formations show working figures with no note; six of them exceed the 22 November returns. Headline strengths carry no claim tag anywhere they appear.
- The note "Kologrivov's command rests on Sokolov alone" is contradicted by Schönhals p. 178 and by the project's own stage 6B reading.
- SOURCE_NOTE's example range "7,750 to 14,200" rests on a figure found only on a popular website.

No application source, data, test, threshold or build was modified, and no repository check was run.

findings.title: Order-of-battle figures attributed to Duffy (1977) that Duffy does not print
findings.subsystem: data.js FORMATIONS strength notes; analysis.js theme 'weakness'; appearance.js COMPOSITION.friant; narrative.js Kienmayer claim note
findings.user_impact:
Visitors are told a named specialist work gives figures it does not print.
- The III Corps detachment's 4,300 (with 830 cavalry) and Friant's 3,470 also appear in the 'weakness' theme, which carries the battle's central argument.
- The IV Column's 13,900 is the column broken on the Pratzen; the Russian wing's 4,800 is 'implied' from it.
- Kienmayer's note says Duffy gives '3,440 foot and 3,440 horse, which make 6,880'.
- Dokhturov's note gives 13,240 infantry.
The drawn strengths of the III Corps detachment, the IV Column and its Russian wing rest on these figures, and derived readings sum plotted strengths.
findings.status: confirmed (on Duffy's OCR text layer, via archive.org full-text search; the lending item's page images cannot be opened here; the same search reproduces exactly the Guard rows that S5.7 read on the owner's photograph)
refs: docs/audit-post8-evidence/sources-oob/ledger.md L07 L08 L10 L20 L22 L26 L27
findings.evidence:
Duffy, text-layer snippets:
- 'Ill Corps, MARSHAL DAVOUT 2nd Div. (3,800 and 9 guns) Gen. Friant'
- '4th Dr. Div. (2,500 and 3 guns) Gen. Bourcier'; in the narrative, 'the supporting dragoon division of Bourcier (2,500 men and 3 guns)'
- 'Advance Guard of 1st Column, Lt.-Gen. Kienmayer (6,780 and 12 light pieces)', and 'this figure, like the following figures, presents the over-optimistic nominal ...'
- '1st Column, Lt.-Gen. Dokhturov (13,650, 40 light and 24 heavy pieces)'
- '4th Column, Lt.-Gens. Miloradovich and Kollowrath (23,900, 52 light and 24 heavy pieces)'; in the narrative, 'an Austro-Russian fourth column of 23,900 infantry'

The map's figures 4,300, 830, 3,470, 3,440, 13,240 and 13,900 have zero hits anywhere in the book. Every gun count agrees: 12 = 9+3; 12; 64; 76. Duffy's IV Column rows add to about 16,065 (derived), not 13,900.
findings.expected: A figure attributed to a named work is printed in it (CLAUDE.md: never invent sources). Where a work is cited but not read, the note does not state what it gives.
findings.observed:
- c_iii: 'Duffy and Smith give 4,300 men present, including 830 cavalry, with 12 guns'
- friant: 'about 3,470 in Duffy and Smith'
- theme: 'some 4,300 men by Duffy's and Smith's count'
- kienmayer: 'Duffy and Smith ..., as transcribed here, give 3,440 foot and 3,440 horse, which make 6,880'
- dok: '13,240 infantry and 250 cavalry with 64 guns (Duffy/Smith)'
- col4: '13,900 infantry with 52 light and 24 heavy guns (Duffy 1977; Smith 1998) ... 23,900 (Chandler, and an older revision of the same order of battle)'
- milo: 'Duffy and Smith imply about 4,800 (13,900 less the Austrian brigades' 9,100)'
findings.remedy:
1. Have Duffy pp. 179-185 read on the page (a loan, or the owner's photograph as for S5.7) and register them.
2. Then, in a data task recorded in CHANGELOG.md, correct each attribution (to Smith only if Smith is read) and settle the working figures with Schönhals, Sokolov and Duffy as the sides.
3. Meanwhile, reword the six notes and the theme so they no longer credit Duffy with numbers absent from his text.
findings.effort: 2-4 h to reword and rehash the claims; 1-2 days for the page reading and the data task
findings.risk: A data change moves check:data's reference and the claims' hashes. Counter ranks and map-layer drop limits may move, as may sim-test's tour stop 4 figures.
findings.validation: test.js (claims); check:data; re-run tools/audit-post8/sources-oob/ia-fts.py; a person reads Duffy's pages
findings.cause_hypothesis: The early correction pass ('Order of battle (Duffy 1977 and Smith 1998, unless a range names others)', CHANGELOG.md:9316) transcribed figures under a joint heading from another compilation or from Smith. 23,900 to 13,900 looks like a digit slip. Kienmayer's 3,440 + 3,440 mixes in Sokolov's 3,440 infantry.

findings.title: The III Corps detachment and the IV Column are drawn below every figure in the sources the project can read, and their notes omit those figures
findings.subsystem: data.js FORMATIONS c_iii, friant, bourcier, col4, milo
findings.user_impact:
The thinness of the right is drawn larger than any readable source has it:
- Bourcier: 830 drawn, against Sokolov's presumed 1,500 and Duffy's 2,500.
- The detachment: 4,300 drawn, against 5,300-6,300.

The IV Column is drawn smaller:
- The column: 13,900 drawn, against about 16,100.
- Its Russian wing: 4,800 drawn, against Schönhals's 6,965.

Visitors cannot see the read figures. Derived readings that sum plotted strengths inherit the gaps (not recomputed here).
findings.evidence:
III Corps:
- Sokolov pp. 188-189 (page images; never registered): Friant 7,037 on 22 November, presumed 3,800; Bourcier 1,900, presumed 1,500; Davout 8,975 / 5,300. The register already quotes the 5,300 from p. 193 (C5.8).
- Sokolov: 'Даву мог располагать не более чем 3 500—4 000 человек из дивизии Фриана и 1 200—1 500 человек из дивизии Бурсье'.
- Thiers p. 310 (C6.17): Friant 'réduite à 6 mille hommes au plus'. No source read gives the note's 'about 6,400'.

IV Column:
- Schönhals p. 177 (page image): 'Summa der ganzen Colonne . 27 5 2 16118 125' (recapitulation 16,115); Russian wing 6,965.
- Sokolov p. 197: '15 900 пех., 300 ка[в]'.
- Duffy's rows: about 16,065 (text layer, derived).
- col4's note lists 12,000 (WarHistory), 17,000 (Napoleon-Empire) and 23,900 (Chandler), but neither read total, although it cites Schönhals for battalion counts.
findings.expected: CLAUDE.md: 'Where sources disagree, keep the disagreement. Prefer primary and specialist sources.' The figures of the sources read appear as sides.
findings.observed: c_iii is 4,300 (Friant 3,470 + Bourcier 830); bourcier's 'about 830 sabres present' names no source; col4 is 13,900 and milo 4,800, with the read totals absent from both notes.
findings.remedy:
Data task, with CHANGELOG records:
1. Register Sokolov pp. 188-189.
2. Name Sokolov's and Schönhals's figures as sides in the notes.
3. Reconsider the working figures (e.g. the IV Column about 16,100; Bourcier 1,500).
4. Re-measure the derived readings and the limits.
findings.effort: 1-2 days (with the first finding's data task)
findings.risk: Moves the plateau holding reading, tour stop 4's figures (held by sim-test), counter ranks and map-layer drop limits
findings.dependencies: Same data task as the Duffy attribution finding

findings.title: Seven formations show a working strength with no note; six exceed the 22 November returns the project reads elsewhere
findings.subsystem: data.js FORMATIONS kellermann, dhautpoul, walther, rivaud, drouet, guard_inf, guard_cav
findings.user_impact: The French Guard cavalry is shown and drawn as about 2,500 men, about 2.4 times the only return read (1,023 horse). This changes the apparent balance of its fight with the Russian Guard cavalry. The cavalry divisions and I Corps' divisions are 7-19% above their 22 November figures, yet strength could only have fallen between 22 November and 2 December.
findings.evidence:
Sokolov page images (archive.org 1799-1805-.-ii):
- p. 193: horse chasseurs 376, Mamelukes 48, horse grenadiers 599, horse artillery 298 (Guard horse 1,023)
- p. 191: Kellermann 2,021 (presumed 1,500)
- p. 190: d'Hautpoul 1,136 (presumed 1,100); Walther 1,340 (presumed 1,200)
- register C5.9: Rivaud 5,216, Drouet 6,318

The map draws 2,500, 2,400, 1,300, 1,500, 6,000 and 7,000, none with a note. Nansouty's 1,600 (Sokolov 1,496 / 1,300) has a note.
findings.expected: Each working figure is labelled, and a read source giving another figure is named (CLAUDE.md: label claims; keep the disagreement).
findings.observed: Bare figures. The only label is SOURCE_NOTE.refs[0]'s 'a figure without a note is this map's', on the sources sheet.
findings.remedy: Data task: give each formation a note with Sokolov's figures (or adopt them), with claims registered.
findings.risk: Same as the previous finding (ranks, derived readings)

findings.title: Headline strength and gun figures carry no claim tag; the compact card shows strength with neither note nor tag
findings.subsystem: app.js compactCard and dossierFormation; tools/step4/statements.js classes
findings.user_impact:
The most visible forces figures, '≈ N men' and the gun count, carry no claim word wherever they appear.
- The compact card, the first view of a selected formation, never shows the strength note. 34 formations show a bare figure; three with a range say 'working figure'.
- Seven formations have no note even in the full dossier.
findings.evidence:
- compactCard: 'else if(str) body+=row("Strength","≈ "+str.toLocaleString("en-GB")+" men"+(f.guns?...))', with no claimTag and no note.
- dossierFormation: 'row("Approximate strength",...)' and 'row("Guns", esc(String(f.guns)))', with no claimTag. Only strengthNote gets one.
- The statement classes cover strings only, so the numbers sit outside the claims inventory.
findings.expected: CLAUDE.md: 'Label claims as fact, disputed, derived, inference, uncertain, or design decision.'
findings.observed: Unlabelled headline numbers on every formation
findings.remedy: Tag the strength row with its note's claim, otherwise with a class claim ('This map's reading' for a working figure). On the compact card, say 'working figure' as it already does for ranges, or link to the note.
findings.risk: Changes compact-card rows (check:visual layouts; the phone cut-text checks)

findings.title: 'Kologrivov's command on 2 December is in Sokolov alone' is contradicted by Schönhals p. 178 and by the project's own stage 6B reading
findings.user_impact: Two places tell visitors that a single modern work supports the commander shown: the Russian Guard cavalry's dossier (tagged 'As a source tells it') and the sources sheet's open questions. Yet a source read on its page since step 4 names him in the battle's order of battle. The stage 6B reading had already logged this as 'a second source for that name'.
findings.evidence:
- Schönhals p. 178 (page image), in 'Ordre de Bataille des verbündeten Heeres in der Schlacht von Austerlitz': 'K. russische Garden | Grossfürst Constantin | Waren am Morgen in Schlachtordnung | GL. Kollowrizow | GM. Jancowitz'.
- Stage 6B reading: 'supports the project's rg_cav commander "Kologrivov" (as "GL. Kollowrizow"): a second source for that name'.
- Duffy p. 184 heading (S5.7): 'Lt.-Gen. of Cavalry Kologrivov'.
- C6.n7 searched with 'Кологрив|Kologri|Kolagri|Kologriw|Колог', which cannot match 'Kollowrizow'.
- Also: the rows decision 213 (b) took from the owner's photograph of Duffy are printed on the same Schönhals page, and 6B had already summed them to 6,730 and 2,900. The rg_inf note credits Duffy alone.
findings.expected: The open question states the sources as read: Sokolov's order of battle; Schönhals's undated table, which puts him over the whole Guard; Duffy's heading.
findings.observed: 'in Sokolov alone, with no source on his page' (rg_cav note); 'which rests on Sokolov alone' (SOURCE_NOTE)
findings.remedy:
In a data task with CHANGELOG records:
1. Reword rg_cav.strengthNote and SOURCE_NOTE.body[5].
2. Cite Schönhals p. 178 for the rows in the rg_inf and rg_cav notes.
3. Widen C6.n7's search patterns.

findings.title: SOURCE_NOTE illustrates disagreement among 'reputable orders of battle' with an I Column range whose low end appears only on a popular website
findings.user_impact: The method statement says reputable orders of battle give the I Column anything from 7,750 to 14,200 men. The sources read here agree within about 10% (12,730-14,000). The statement overstates the uncertainty and gives a web figure the authority of 'reputable' and 'returns'.
findings.status: confirmed (no source read gives 7,750; its web origin is known only from a search result's summary)
findings.evidence:
- Schönhals: 12,730 / 13,730 (page images)
- Duffy: 13,650 (text layer)
- Sokolov: 13,800 + 200 Cossacks (page image)
- Web search: 7,752 on military-review.com (HTTP 503 when fetched); about 14,200 on a fan site.
findings.expected: Only reputable sources are called reputable; an illustrative range is sourced.
findings.observed: 'Dokhturov's I Column is given as anything from 7,750 to 14,200 men'; 'other returns range from 7,750 to 14,200'
findings.remedy: Use the read sources' range, or a figure genuinely disputed among read sources (e.g. the IV Column, about 16,000 against Duffy's 23,900). Correct the dok note's 'returns'.

findings.title: Army-total notes omit figures the project read and credit Duffy with a total he does not give
findings.user_impact: The army totals' stated ranges look narrower and better sourced than the sources read show.
findings.status: confirmed (register readings; Duffy on the text layer)
findings.evidence:
- gqg.note's 'Other accounts range from 65,000 to 75,000' omits Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky 1844 p. 171, 'до 90,000' (C5.26, page image), and Duffy's own 'effective force ... as little as 60,000' (text layer).
- ahq.army's 'about 85,400 ... (Duffy 1977; Smith 1998)': Duffy gives 'between 80,000 and 87,000 troops, with 278 pieces' (text layer).
- The Bulletin's 105,000 goes unremarked.
findings.expected: Ranges include the figures read; an attribution matches the work.
findings.remedy: Reword the two notes with the read figures. Attribute 85,400 to its actual source, or replace it with Duffy's range.

findings.title: Stronger or earlier sources uncredited, and two locator slips
findings.user_impact: Small loss of evidential strength and traceability
findings.evidence:
- Decision 202 (b) cites only Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky; the 30th Bulletin (grade A) p. 450 also says 'Il avait avec lui la division Friant et les dragons de la division du général Bourcier'.
- Duffy prints working figures the map calls its own or leaves unsourced: V Corps 12,700 with 20 guns; I Corps 13,000; Langeron 11,700; Bagration 13,700 with 42; Liechtenstein 5,375.
- Kamensky's 'about 2,000 each' is credited to Duffy only, although Schönhals and Sokolov (both read) print it; Schönhals's brace also includes Kursk.
- Fieffé's locator says 'footnote', but the passage is body text on p. 17.
- The ru_musk coat cites the grenadier table (Viskovatov p. 196) without the musketeer extension on pp. 229-230.
findings.expected: The strongest source read is cited; locators are exact.
findings.remedy: Fold into the next data task.

findings.title: Owner-decided force claims are consistent with their decisions
findings.user_impact: None beyond the decisions' stated trade-offs
findings.evidence:
- 184: Kienmayer 6,340 (Schönhals p. 177 page image) and Sokolov's 6,380 (p. 194).
- 202 (b): Bourcier up from Raigern with Friant (Mikhailovsky-Danilevsky p. 178; the 30th Bulletin).
- 210 (c): Guard infantry commander not established (Sokolov pp. 199-200).
- 213 (b): 4,430 and 2,900 match Schönhals's rows; the corps is kept at 10,500 against 7,330 drawn, which is acknowledged.
- 243 (a): Salligny's letter quoted exactly (Alombert t. IV p. 183); applying it to 2 December is labelled an inference.
findings.observed: It does. Only the Duffy sentence in Kienmayer's note and the Kologrivov wording conflict with sources; both are covered by the findings above.
